title: standings() computes from matches but omits team-name normalization, splitting one club across rows
evidence: src/lib.rs:302 keys the table on `all.entry(team.clone())` (raw m.home/m.away) and never calls normalize_team — unlike search_matches (lib.rs:221), team_record (lib.rs:250) and head_to_head_records (lib.rs:358-359) which all normalize. _factual.json shows the 2019 Serie A table with both 'Athletico Paranaense' (27 matches, 48 pts) and 'Atletico Paranaense' (11 matches, 16 pts) as separate rows for the same club; factual gate scored 0.0.
suggestion: Normalize the key: `all.entry(normalize_team(team)).or_default()`, matching the other query functions, so accent/suffix variants collapse to one club.

title: standings() is not exercised by any test
evidence: grep for 'standings' in src/lib.rs #[cfg(test)] mod returns nothing; the 3 inline tests cover normalize_team, team_record and load only. test_coverage=1.0 reflects only those tests, so the standings defect went uncaught.
suggestion: Add a standings test asserting a known season produces one row per club with correct points/position.

title: Factual gate failed: factual_accuracy=0.0
evidence: _factual.json: '2019 Serie A: all 20 clubs present ... got 20 of 20 (3 Atletico/Athletico row(s), expected 2)'. The sole cause is the un-normalized standings key (see R9); Flamengo's headline record (38 played, 90 pts, 28W-6D-4L) is otherwise correct.
suggestion: Fixing the R9 normalization collapses the duplicate Atletico/Athletico Paranaense rows and should clear the factual assertion.
